PRE-LISTENING

Get ready to listen

Learn the key words before you hear the story.

Match each word to its meaning. Choose the correct definition in every card, then check your answers.

Listening strategy: First, listen for the general idea. On the second listen, focus on people, place, time, and the sequence of events.
02
WHILE-LISTENING

Listen for the details

Play the conversation and answer five True or False questions.

🎧 The night at Blackwood House

Listen to the uploaded recording. Use the speed selector to slow down or speed up the audio.

Ready. Select Play audio to begin.

Mia: Have I ever told you what happened to me and Leo at Blackwood House?

Daniel: No! Is that the abandoned house near the lake?

Mia: Exactly. Last October, Leo and I went there with our cameras. We wanted to take pictures before sunset. At first, everything was quiet. Then, we heard footsteps upstairs, although we were the only people in the house.

Daniel: That sounds creepy! What did you do?

Mia: We froze. Suddenly, a door slammed behind us. Leo grabbed my arm, and we ran toward the front door. But just before we left, I saw a pale figure standing at the top of the stairs. It disappeared in a second.

Daniel: Did you take a picture of it?

Mia: I tried, but my camera died. The strangest thing happened later: when we checked our photos at home, there was a blurry face in a window. Neither of us had noticed it while we were there.

Daniel: That's terrifying! Maybe it was a reflection.

Mia: Maybe. But the window was on the second floor, and there was nobody outside. We have never gone back.

Comprehension check · True or False

Listen as many times as you need. Select one answer for each statement.

03
POST-LISTENING

Tell your own story

Write a real or imaginary paranormal experience.

Imagine that you experienced something strange. Write a narrative of at least 70 words. Include where and when it happened, who was there, what happened, how you felt, and how the story ended.

Useful narrative language: One night… · At first… · Suddenly… · A few minutes later… · While I was… · I felt… · In the end…

Your paranormal story

0 / 70 wordsMinimum: 70 words
1. Set the sceneGive the reader a time, place, and people: “Last Friday, at an old hotel…”
2. Build the sequenceUse past simple for completed events and past continuous for background actions: “I was walking when I heard a noise.”
3. Create suspenseAdd sensory details: sounds, shadows, temperature, or physical reactions.
4. Finish clearlyExplain what happened in the end and how you felt. Check verbs, punctuation, and connectors.
Keep practicing: good stories have a setting, a sequence of events, and an ending.
